qa.question:
For the financial year ended 31 December 2025, the group reported revenue of RM2.01 
million. According to management, the improvement was supported by higher quarry 
production and improving sales demand as operations progressed. The group also reported 
further development of the marble quarry, increased production output and expansion into 
the Middle Eastern market.  
 
(Source: company annual report) 
 
The group has been transitioning from its traditional ground calcium carbonate (GCC) 
operations towards marble quarrying, with repair works at the marble quarry 
recommencing more than six years ago since June 2020. 
 
(i) 
Can management provide a breakdown of FY2025 revenue between marble 
blocks and GCC? How has the revenue mix evolved over the past three 
financial years? 
 
(ii) 
How many quarry faces are currently in active production of marble blocks? 
What are the principal constraints on scaling production, including quarry 
development, equipment, labour, processing capacity, logistics or working 
capital? 
 
(iii) 
What progress has the group made in developing its Middle Eastern market, 
in terms of customer acquisition, confirmed orders, shipment volumes and 
revenue contribution? To what extent have the ongoing conflicts in the 
Middle East affected customer demand, order fulfilment, shipping, logistics 
costs or payment risk?

The group’s production projections for marble blocks have been materially reduced over 
successive annual reports. In the 2023 annual report, management projected annual 
production of 30,000 tonnes in FY2026. This was reduced to 15,000 tonnes in the 2024 

annual report and further to 750 tonnes in the 2025 annual report, representing a 97.5% 
reduction from the original projection. 
 
 
(Compiled from company annual reports)  
 
(i) 
What were the principal factors behind the successive downward revisions 
to the quarry’s production projections? To what extent were these 
attributable to technical or geological constraints, equipment and 
infrastructure limitations, operational execution, market demand or other 
factors? Which of the original assumptions relied upon in the board’s 
approval to enter the marble business have proved unrealistic?  
 
(ii) 
Given the scale of the revisions, what guidance and intervention has the 
board provided to management? How does the board monitor progress 
against production targets?  
 
(iii) 
In light of the substantial reduction in projected production, has the board 
reassessed the quarry’s commercial viability and the group’s original 
investment thesis? What minimum return thresholds and performance 
milestones must the quarry meet to justify further investment, and what 
specific conditions would trigger a decision to suspend additional capital 
expenditure or exit the project?

The board is of the opinion that the group is able to operate as a going concern1 and are 
able to meet their obligations as and when they fall due, and that the group’s working capital 
is sufficient to meet their present requirements for at least the next twelve months.  
 
1 As at 31 December 2025, the group’s and the company’s current liabilities exceeded its current assets by 
RM6.13 million (2024: RM12.47 million) and RM8.84 million (2024: RM7.08 million) respectively.  

This assessment is based, among other factors, on expected revenue from the sale of 
limestone and marble products to customers in South-East Asia, which the board expects to 
be sufficient to cover the group’s operating costs..  
 
(i) 
Given that the auditors have issued a disclaimer of opinion, can 
management provide shareholders with the revenue projections 
underpinning the board’s going-concern assessment, including the 
expected sales volumes, average selling prices and timing of revenue 
recognition for limestone and marble products? With approximately ten 
months of FY2026 elapsed, has the group achieved its projected revenue to 
date? 
 
(ii) 
Has management identified any non-core quarry land or underutilised 
equipment, such as crusher plants, that could be monetised to improve the 
group’s liquidity?  
 
As at 31 December 2025, the group reported total current liabilities of RM13.88 million, 
including lease liabilities, but held only RM89,651 in cash. 
 
 
The independent auditor has issued a disclaimer of opinion on the following bases: 
- 
the appropriateness of the going concern assumption; 
- 
the impairment assessment of the group’s property, plant and equipment; and 
- 
the impairment assessment of the company’s investments in subsidiaries and amounts due from 
subsidiaries. 

(Source: company annual report; emphasis added) 
 
(iii) 
Can management provide a breakdown of how these current liabilities are 
expected to be settled, particularly trade payables, other payables and 
accrued operating expenses? 
 
(iv) 
Has the board considered whether a rights issue would be a prudent and 
viable means of strengthening the group’s liquidity and balance sheet?
